title: Irrationality of nth Roots of Non-Perfect Powers

problemStatement.formal: For n ≥ 2 and m ≥ 1, if m is not a perfect nth power (no integer k satisfies k^n = m), then m^(1/n) is irrational.
problemStatement.plain: The nth root of any positive integer that is not a perfect nth power is irrational. This generalizes √2 irrationality to all roots.
whyMatters: Natural generalization of the classical √2 irrationality proof
Subsumes infinitely many specific irrationality results (√2, √3, ∛2, etc.)
Demonstrates Mathlib's irrational_nrt_of_notint_nrt as a powerful abstraction

proven: General theorem: m^(1/n) irrational when m is not a perfect nth power
Not-an-integer lemma: m^(1/n) not integer when m not a perfect nth power
Converse: m = k^n implies m^(1/n) = k (rational)
